courses.title: Weekly Food Cost Control
courses.subtitle: Calculate, track, and reduce food cost every week

lessons.title: Calculating Actual Food Cost
lessons.summary: Actual food use equals beginning inventory plus purchases minus ending inventory. Most restaurants fail because they don't calculate food cost properly or frequently enough. Weekly tracking is the foundation of cost control.

source.title: 4 Steps to Calculate Restaurant Food Cost

lessons.title: Tracking Daily Sales by Category
lessons.summary: Track gross sales by category -- food, bottle beer, draft beer, wine, liquor, and merchandise. This breakdown feeds your weekly prime cost and budget variance report, giving managers the data to calculate food cost accurately each week.

source.title: Why You Should Track Daily Sales in Your Restaurant

lessons.title: Budget Variance and Manager Ownership
lessons.summary: When managers present their own food cost numbers and identify variances, the dynamic shifts: instead of the owner interrogating, the manager owns the problem. A manager who says 'I found the problem, I fixed it, and here is what remains' is operating at a higher level.

source.title: Understanding and Utilizing a Weekly Restaurant Budget Variance Report

quiz.question: What is the formula for actual food use?
choices: Total sales minus total purchases
Beginning inventory plus purchases minus ending inventory
Ending inventory minus beginning inventory
Total purchases divided by total sales
quiz.explanation: Actual food use equals beginning inventory plus purchases minus ending inventory. This captures everything sold, wasted, spoiled, or otherwise removed from stock during the period.

quiz.question: Why should managers present their own food cost numbers at weekly meetings?
choices: It saves the owner time on data entry
It shifts accountability so the manager owns the problem and the solution
It is only required by health code
It replaces the need for inventory counts
quiz.explanation: When managers present their own numbers, they own the variance. Instead of the owner saying 'what happened,' the manager arrives with the problem, the fix, and a plan for what remains.

courses.operatingAssignment: Pull this week's beginning inventory, purchases, and ending inventory. Calculate actual food cost percentage. Identify the top three dollar variances and bring them to your next weekly review with a proposed corrective action for each.

courses.title: Labor Cost and Scheduling
courses.subtitle: Schedule on budget, track hours and dollars, and control overtime

lessons.title: The Restaurant Payroll Guardian
lessons.summary: Control labor costs by scheduling for both dollars and hours, not just filling shifts. Give your management team the ability to know exactly what people should be working before the schedule goes live. Scheduling software that shows sales forecasts alongside labor spend is essential.

source.title: Master Restaurant Kitchen Systems for Seamless Operations

lessons.title: Scheduling on Budget Each Week
lessons.summary: Set a labor budget to hit your ideal labor cost for the year. Use scheduling software so you can see your sales, hours, and dollar amounts before you schedule. Go into each week on budget by building the schedule against a target, not reacting after payroll runs.

source.title: Essential Tactics to Control Restaurant Labor Cost

quiz.question: What should you see in scheduling software before publishing a schedule?
choices: Only employee availability
Sales forecasts, scheduled hours, and projected labor dollars
Just the number of shifts filled
Only the previous week's actual hours
quiz.explanation: Scheduling software should show sales forecasts alongside hours and dollars so you can go into each week on budget, not discover overruns after the fact.

quiz.question: What is the Restaurant Payroll Guardian approach?
choices: Hiring a dedicated payroll clerk
Scheduling for both dollars and hours against a budget target
Cutting staff after every slow night
Outsourcing all scheduling to corporate
quiz.explanation: The Restaurant Payroll Guardian is a system for scheduling against a labor budget -- tracking both hours and dollars so the management team knows exactly what people should be working before the week starts.

courses.operatingAssignment: Before publishing next week's schedule, calculate your labor budget target. Compare projected hours and dollars against that target. Identify any day where projected labor exceeds the budget and adjust before the schedule goes live.

courses.title: Inventory and Recipe Costing
courses.subtitle: Recipe cards, shelf-to-sheet inventory, and ideal vs. actual usage

lessons.title: Why Recipe Costing Cards Matter
lessons.summary: Without recipe costing cards, you cannot know your true cost per plate. While manual cards are time-consuming and quickly outdated, food management software keeps recipe costs current by syncing invoices, inventory, and menu mix automatically.

lessons.title: Ideal vs. Actual Product Usage
lessons.summary: The most powerful output of food and beverage software is ideal versus actual product usage. Because you take inventory, enter invoices, maintain recipe costs, and tie in POS data, you can see exactly where usage exceeds what should have been used -- and investigate the gap.

source.title: Kitchen Systems Every Restaurant Needs to Use to Lower Food Cost

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of software-based recipe costing over spreadsheets?
choices: Spreadsheets are more accurate
Software automatically updates recipe costs when invoice prices change
Spreadsheets update in real time
Software eliminates the need for inventory
quiz.explanation: When you use food management software, uploading invoices automatically updates recipe cards, order guides, and inventory valuations -- keeping everything current without the 40-100 hours of manual spreadsheet maintenance.

quiz.question: What does 'ideal vs. actual product usage' reveal?
choices: How much product you ordered
The gap between what should have been used based on sales and what was actually used
The total cost of your menu
How many recipes you have entered
quiz.explanation: Ideal vs. actual usage compares what your POS says you sold (and therefore should have used) against what inventory shows you actually consumed. The gap highlights waste, portioning issues, theft, or recipe errors.

courses.operatingAssignment: Pick your top five selling menu items. Verify that each has a current recipe costing card with accurate ingredient prices. For any item missing a card or with outdated pricing, build or update it this week.

courses.title: Accountability Systems
courses.subtitle: Define the job, set the standard, and verify the work

lessons.title: Foundational Systems Change Everything
lessons.summary: There is no finish line in the restaurant business -- but when foundational systems are in place, it changes your world. You shift from working in the business to working on it: budgets, marketing, developing managers, and holding them accountable.

source.title: How Restaurant Owner Used Coaching to Save Her Business

lessons.title: Training and Systems for Manager Accountability
lessons.summary: First learn, then train your managers on your system, your process, your way. Step-by-step procedures that define how things get done are the foundation. Then put systems in place to hold managers accountable to those standards.

source.title: Restaurant Owner Success Depends on This

quiz.question: What must happen before you can hold a manager accountable?
choices: Threaten consequences for poor performance
Define the job, the method, and the required standard, then train to it
Simply tell them to do better
Wait until the end of the quarter to review
quiz.explanation: Accountability starts with clarity: define the job, the method, and the standard. Then train the manager on your system and your way. Only after that foundation exists can you hold someone answerable for execution.

quiz.question: What shifts when foundational operating systems are in place?
choices: The owner can work on budgets, marketing, and team development instead of firefighting
The restaurant no longer needs managers
Food cost automatically drops to zero
The owner never needs to visit the restaurant
quiz.explanation: With foundational systems in place, the owner shifts from being trapped in daily operations to working on the business: budgets, marketing, leading the team, developing managers, and holding them accountable.

courses.operatingAssignment: Choose one recurring management task (e.g., daily line check, weekly inventory count, nightly close procedure). Write a clear step-by-step standard for it. Train the responsible manager this week and schedule a verification checkpoint.

courses.title: Delegation and Trust
courses.subtitle: Stop doing everything yourself and develop the next generation

lessons.title: Trust and Verify
lessons.summary: Let managers struggle and figure things out. They may surprise you. Your job is to develop the next generation of leaders. If you keep doing everything yourself, you will never step back, and the restaurant will never reach its full potential.

source.title: How Restaurant Owners Can Make Sure Their Team Can Handle It

lessons.title: Implementing One System at a Time
lessons.summary: Pick any system you can handle -- whether standardizing a bar drawer count, recipe costing cards, shelf-to-sheet inventory, scheduling on budget, or ideal vs. actual usage. Start with one, implement it, and build from there rather than trying to change everything at once.

source.title: How to Manage a Restaurant 5 Tips from Successful Independent Owners

quiz.question: What does 'trust and verify' mean in delegation?
choices: Trust blindly and never check results
Delegate the task, let them work through it, then verify the outcome
Do the work yourself and have someone watch
Only trust senior managers with any task
quiz.explanation: Trust and verify means giving the manager ownership of the task, allowing them room to struggle and learn, and then verifying the results. This builds capability while maintaining accountability.

quiz.question: Why should you implement one system at a time?
choices: Multiple systems are always contradictory
It is easier to build consistency, train properly, and verify results before adding complexity
There is only one system that matters
Managers cannot learn more than one thing per year
quiz.explanation: Picking one system, implementing it properly, training the team, and verifying it works creates a solid foundation. Trying to change everything at once leads to incomplete adoption and no real accountability.

courses.operatingAssignment: Identify one task you currently do yourself that a manager could own. Write out the process, hand it off this week, and schedule a verification check-in within 7 days. Document what you observe.

courses.title: Leadership and Culture
courses.subtitle: Build a proactive culture where the team knows what success looks like

lessons.title: Building a Proactive Restaurant Culture
lessons.summary: Build a leadership team that knows what success looks like, has the tools to get there, and is held accountable to results. That trust is what gives you the freedom to step away. It starts with leadership structure, clear expectations, and consistent follow-through.

source.title: Can You Manage a Restaurant Remotely?

lessons.title: Building Guest Relationships as a Manager
lessons.summary: When customers start asking for the manager by name rather than the owner, you know the culture is working. Touching tables and building relationships creates loyal customers who return. As a manager, those bonds are a sign of real leadership on the floor.

source.title: The Right and Wrong Ways to Touch Tables in a Restaurant

quiz.question: What defines a proactive restaurant culture?
choices: The owner makes every decision personally
The team knows what success looks like, has the tools, and is held accountable to results
Everyone works longer hours
Only senior staff attend meetings
quiz.explanation: A proactive culture means the leadership team knows the standards, has the tools and training to achieve them, and is held accountable. This trust is what eventually gives the owner freedom to step back.

quiz.question: What is a sign that floor leadership culture is working?
choices: The owner handles every guest complaint personally
Guests start asking for the manager by name, not just the owner
No one touches tables during service
The manager avoids the dining room
quiz.explanation: When guests ask for the manager by name, it shows the manager has built real relationships on the floor. That personal connection creates loyalty and demonstrates leadership beyond the owner.

courses.operatingAssignment: During your next three shifts, make a point to touch every table in your section. Track the number of guest interactions and note any feedback. At the end of the week, identify one guest relationship you strengthened and how.
